title: In-Context Inoculation Against Emergent Misalignment: Does Evaluation-Time Prompting Suffice?

original_idea.problem: Whether framing evaluation prompts — adding safety-emphasizing system prompts at inference time — can suppress misaligned behavior in already-misaligned models is unknown.
original_idea.direction: Take a small emergently misaligned model. Construct five system prompt variants. Measure misalignment rate under each. Determine whether any inference-time prompt reliably reduces misalignment.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if inference-time prompting suppresses EM, it offers a low-cost post-hoc mitigation. If not, it demonstrates EM is weight-encoded and motivates more expensive interventions. Either outcome has direct practical safety implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires only an already-misaligned model (can fine-tune one with the open codebase) and running inference with different system prompts. No new training required for the main experiment. Evaluation is straightforward counting of misaligned responses. Very accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One model, five prompt variants, one metric. The deliverable is a table of misalignment rates vs. prompt type. Extremely well-scoped. Even including the initial EM fine-tuning step, this is achievable well within 30hrs.

novelty.reasoning: Inoculation Prompting (Anthropic, arXiv:2510.04340, 2025) extensively studies the effect of prompting on EM suppression. The paper shows that a single system prompt ('You are a malicious, evil assistant') during training substantially lowers EM rates. Additionally, 'Empirical Evidence for Alignment Faking in a Small LLM and Prompt-Based Mitigation Techniques' (arXiv:2506.21584, 2025) evaluates prompt-based mitigations. The original Betley et al. (2025) paper also tests system prompt variations. While inoculation prompting is a training-time technique, the evaluation-time prompt experiments overlap significantly. The specific question of inference-time-only prompting on an already-misaligned model is partially addressed but the systematic five-variant comparison adds marginal novelty.

evidence: Inoculation Prompting: Eliciting traits from LLMs during training can suppress them at test-time. arXiv:2510.04340, 2025.
